NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline

Deliverable 1 — Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model · Draft v5.2

New XP Technologies Limited

8 October 2026 · Confidential · Internal baseline document

Status and conventions

Status: Draft v5.2 (8 October 2026) carries the three changes v5.0 / v5.1 made to v4.0 — (1) the per-project return receiver group is removed: sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group, and a return or hop leg inherits its attribution from its parent leg (D13); (2) RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT carries explicit wallet fields (account_kind, network, address) beside the bank reference (D14); (3) FACILITATING_ENTITY is renamed PARTNER_ENTITY, and the partner's collection endpoints are merged into one COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT table owned by the partner entity (D15; rename pending NPL confirmation) — and adds the four decisions of the review of the v5.1 draft on 8 October 2026: (4) SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION payout details follow the account's kind (D16); (5) DISBURSEMENT_LINE.deal_id, required when the paid receiver is group-less (D17); (6) a nullable rail on COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, required before a bank endpoint is active (D18); (7) an endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection method (D19). Everything else carries over unchanged. Supersedes v5.1, v5.0 and v4.0 in full. This baseline is an internal New XP document; the client deliverables are derived from it.

Convention: all monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals; every table carries created_at / created_by; audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4) and apply to all master data. Derived figures (client balance, group entitlement, offsets, custody) are views over postings and deals — never stored.

Six diagrams across four domains, one schema: 54 tables and 4 views. In each diagram, entities defined in another diagram appear with no attributes and name that diagram. Relationship lines run from the referenced row to the row that stores the foreign key; ||--o{ is composition (the parent owns the child), ||..o{ a reference or a polymorphic link resolved by a type column plus an id. Section 6 lists what changed since v4.0; Appendix A reconciles the model with the FRS; Appendix B is the data dictionary.

1 · Configuration domain

A Project (= client) owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, registrations and rebate terms hang off it. Counterparty receivers are organised in receiver groups, the unit entitlement is tracked on, and each receiving entity holds one or more accounts with a currency and rail.

Diagram 1a. PARTNER_CONFIG, PARTNER_PAIR, SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION are defined in Diagram 1b.

Diagram 1b. PROJECT, CURRENCY_PAIR, SENDER, RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT are defined in Diagram 1a.

Notes

  • A Project (= client) owns its configuration. Counterparty receivers sit in receiver groups: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver belongs to exactly one group. Entitlement is tracked per group, so payouts within a group are ordinary settlement and only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
  • A Receiver has a kind: counterparty for a client receiver; sender_return stands for a sender so refunds use the ordinary payout path and the partner's destination approval; partner_transit stands for a partner's collection endpoint so the hop of a two-leg route is an ordinary payout. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group (group_id is null). They never appear on forward deals or allow lists — both validate kind = counterparty — and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays them, so no entitlement moves between groups on a refund or a hop. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not a group (D13).
  • A receiving entity holds one or more accounts, each with a currency and rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). An account is a bank account or a wallet (account_kind): a bank account carries bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet carries network and address explicitly, mirroring the partner-side COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, so addresses can be checksum-validated, checked against the rail, and found when the same address is registered with two partners. Registrations and payout lines point at the account. No table stores actual bank details: bank_details_ref points at the external store.
  • Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner's markup is visible; partner_markup_pct is known only for market_plus partners.
  • A partner operates through one or more legal vehicles (PARTNER_ENTITY: PT-tour, PT Global Inc); the deal stamps the vehicle at quote so paperwork names the right company. Each vehicle owns the endpoints a sender can pay into (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT): kind = bank with a currency and bank_details_ref, or kind = wallet with network and address. The partner side therefore mirrors the client side — PARTNER_CONFIG → PARTNER_ENTITY → COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT as RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (D15). An endpoint also carries a nullable rail: a bank endpoint must have it before it becomes active, and a wallet may leave it null but must match network when it is set (D18); the endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method (D19). Cash-in has no endpoint record; instructions live on the deal. Cash collections round to the nearest 100 / 500 / 1000 units by currency (CURRENCY_PAIR.cash_rounding_unit).
  • Destination approval is per partner: SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION is an account of the project's receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying the partner's approval status and the payout details the partner holds. Those details follow the account's kind: bank_details_ref for a bank account, network and address for a wallet (D16). SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it; neither holds money. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance only and never a payout destination.
  • OWN_WALLET exists for rerouting and pass-through (AQN-LT-Sub is an own wallet at Aquanow); PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. INTRODUCER / REFERRAL_RULE record referral commissions NPL pays; PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records rebates a partner pays NPL.

2 · Rates domain

Diagram 2. RATE_SOURCE, CURRENCY_PAIR are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_PAIR in 1b; DEAL, CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION in 3a.

Notes

  • The rate comparison for the day is created lazily by the first deal that needs it, one per partner × pair × date, and reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.
  • A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate. Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
  • Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.

3 · Deal lifecycle domain

3a · Deal group, legs, collection, conversion, reroute, balance conversion

Diagram 3a. PROJECT, SENDER, RECEIVER_GROUP, OWN_WALLET, COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY, RECEIVER are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_PAIR, PARTNER_ENTITY, FEE_STRUCTURE, PARTNER_CONFIG, COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT in 1b; MARKET_RATE, PARTNER_RATE_VERSION in 2; DISBURSEMENT_RETURN in 3b.

3b · Disbursement, return, confirmation, fees, referrals and rebates

Diagram 3b. PROJECT, RECEIVER, REFERRAL_RULE are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG, SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY, SETTLEMENT_RAIL, SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION, PARTNER_REBATE_RULE in 1b; DEAL, BALANCE_CONVERSION in 3a.

Derived views (never stored)

ViewDefinition
CLIENT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency)CLIENT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency) = Σ conversions’ actual_out booked at that partner (deal legs and balance conversions, target side) − Σ balance conversions’ amount_in (source side) + Σ returned amounts − Σ released disbursement totals. Carries rounding dust below one unit.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency)GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency) = Σ client_net of converted legs (forward and return) attributed to the group ± entitlement re-attributions − Σ DISBURSEMENT_LINE.amount on lines whose disbursing deal is attributed to the group + Σ returned amounts on those lines. A payout to a group-less receiver debits the group of the leg that pays it, read from DISBURSEMENT_LINE.deal_id (v5.0 D13; D17 makes the paying leg a stored column). Σ over a project's groups = Σ CLIENT_BALANCE over partners, per currency.
OFFSET(group, currency)OFFSET(group, currency) = GROUP_ENTITLEMENT; positive = owed, negative = holding another group's flow. Arises only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group (v5.0); zero by construction in a single-group project. Carries Management approval and tighter aging.
CUSTODY(own_wallet)CUSTODY(own_wallet) = Σ collections into the own wallet under open reroutes + Σ recovered dues resting there − Σ forwarded; each row with deal, reason, age. The standing control on contingency holding.

Notes

  • Every deal belongs to a deal group. DEAL_GROUP is the client-facing instruction: the pair as the sender sees it, the sender rate, fee, reference and entry mode. A plain single-partner deal is a group of one leg; a route that needs two partners (INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton) has two forward legs; a rejected payout is unwound with a return leg.
  • Legs. leg_type forward or return; funding_source collection, prior_leg (leg 2 of a route, no collection) or returned_disbursement (a return leg). Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg. Attribution is to the receiver group: set at quote on the first forward leg, inherited by leg n of a route from leg n−1 and by a return leg from its parent leg. The receiver is optional until settlement.
  • Two entry modes as before: collect-first legs are born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; quote-first legs carry sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late decision. An estimate-first mode gives an indicative figure and prices at conversion.
  • Conversion has exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION. The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion. Amounts are truncated to whole units at conversion; the dropped fraction (rounding_residual) stays client money in the balance and pays out when it reaches a whole unit. NPL's margin is captured at conversion and is never again at risk from a return or a forward.
  • Balance conversion is NPL converting a client's held balance (5K SGD → USDT to fund a 15K USDT payout): Finance-initiated, Management-approved, no sender, receiver or collection, same rate machinery, markup by FEE_DECISION. It names the receiver group it serves; ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION moves that group's entitlement to the new currency, and any excess over the group's entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
  • Reroute is the only way partner or partner entity change after quote. Forwarding is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues: NPL nets what the alternate partner owes it (EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE) against the funds forwarded, within the outstanding receivable, with the partner's agreement recorded. Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.
  • One settlement model: DISBURSEMENT drains one partner's holding into one or many DISBURSEMENT_LINEs, in whole units. Under disburse_policy to_zero the balance after release is less than one unit; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project's exposure cap.
  • A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's attributed group is an offset, created by the same action, with Management approval and tighter aging. A line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver is never an offset: those receivers have no group, and the line debits the group of the leg it names in deal_id (D13, D17).
  • Rejected payout. When the receiving or intermediary bank rejects a transfer, DISBURSEMENT_RETURN records the returned amount, bank fee and reason; the line's outcome becomes returned, a reversing ledger transaction puts the money back into the client's balance and the paying leg's group entitlement, and BANK_FEE_EVENT books the bounce fee. The money then stays in balance for later payouts, or funds a return leg — attributed to the same group — that converts back and pays the sender's return receiver.
  • Fee decisions. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved decision on a single subject: markup applied or waived on a return leg or balance conversion, a network-fee override on a refund, a bank-fee treatment override on one settlement. Standing rules stay in FEE_STRUCTURE and FEE_OVERRIDE.
  • CONFIRMATION is full or short; a short confirmation opens a SHORTFALL topped up by a later disbursement. Rounding differences no longer land here. REFERRAL_ACCRUAL and PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL accrue per deal under their rules; rebates are reconciled monthly against the partner's statement.

4 · Ledger & controls domain

Diagram 4. OWN_WALLET, RECEIVER, SENDER, INTRODUCER are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG in 1b; COLLECTION, CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION, REROUTE in 3a; DISBURSEMENT, DISBURSEMENT_RETURN, CONFIRMATION, BANK_FEE_EVENT, REFERRAL_ACCRUAL, PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL in 3b.

Notes

  • Client due balances are held as one account per project × partner × currency (CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.DUE); group entitlement is a view, not an account. holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity.
  • Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver, and withholding on a reroute is not a separate event because the margin is always captured by whichever partner converts.
  • Recover dues on a reroute posts own-wallet cash against the earnings receivable at the partner: company money on both sides, no income.
  • Transaction sources: Collection, Conversion, BalanceConversion, Disbursement, DisbursementReturn, Confirmation, BankFeeEvent, Reroute, Referral, Rebate, Adjustment. Account purposes include PAYABLE, REFERRAL_PAYABLE and REBATE_RECEIVABLE; ADVANCE does not exist. Cost components include referral and rounding.
  • APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG and RECORD_LOCK are modelled once and apply to all master data. Approver ≠ initiator on every approval; Operations never sees derived economics. Approval actions include refund_to_third_party, cross_group_payout, balance_conversion, recover_dues. cross_group_payout never fires on a line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver.

5 · Invariants (enforced at write time)

  1. Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency.
  2. Ledger tables are append-only; corrections are reversing transactions.
  3. No custody in the normal path: CL.OWN.*.HELD may only be debited by a collection on a deal with an approved REROUTE; the custody aging view is the standing control.
  4. Disburse to less than one unit: under disburse_policy = to_zero a DISBURSEMENT pays whole units and leaves only rounding dust; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project’s exposure cap (Q5, Q8).
  5. Priced once, per leg: a leg’s pricing fields are write-once after priced_at; a re-quote is a new leg or a new deal group.
  6. Partner fixed at quote, per leg: partner_pair_id / partner_entity_id change only through an approved REROUTE. A collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity (v5.1, D15). Its kind must match the leg’s collection_method — wallet for crypto, bank for bank, no endpoint for cash (v5.2, D19). A COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint; a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).
  7. Entitlement conservation: Σ GROUP_ENTITLEMENT over a project’s groups = Σ CLIENT_BALANCE over partners, per currency, including balance-conversion re-attributions. Return and hop legs preserve this because they inherit the parent leg’s group (D13). Since v5.2 every payout line resolves to a group — the paid receiver’s for a counterparty, the paying leg’s via deal_id otherwise — so this is checkable mechanically (D17).
  8. Destination approval precedes collection: a quote-first deal cannot leave Inquiry unless at least one account in the entitled group has an approved SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION with the chosen partner.
  9. Approver ≠ initiator on every APPROVAL; Operations never receives derived-economics fields.
  10. Every balance shown anywhere is a sum over postings or deals.
  11. A collect-first deal requires an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry for its sender and group (Q1).
  12. A return leg pays the sender_return RECEIVER linked to the parent leg’s sender, unless a Management-approved exception with a reason names another approved receiver.
  13. The failed forward line is reversed before a return leg opens, so entitlement and balance are correct at the return conversion.
  14. A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a balance conversion.
  15. A recovery on a reroute cannot exceed the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE at that partner; the alternate partner’s expected conversion is computed on the net amount forwarded.
  16. Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver (Q13).
  17. Offsets arise only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to a different group, and carry Management approval and tighter aging. A project with one group never has an offset; within a group nothing is tracked beyond an informational tally (v5.0).
  18. A RECEIVER has a group_id if and only if kind = counterparty. Forward legs and the sender allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only. A return leg inherits receiver_group_id from its parent leg; leg n of a route inherits it from leg n−1 (v5.0, D13).
  19. A DISBURSEMENT_LINE paying a group-less receiver (sender_return, partner_transit) carries deal_id; the paying leg’s group is a stored fact, never inferred (v5.2, D17).

6 · What changed from v4.0

Three changes came in v5.0 / v5.1 (7 October 2026): the per-project return receiver group is removed (D13), RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT gains explicit wallet fields (D14), and the partner's collection side is restructured — FACILITATING_ENTITY becomes PARTNER_ENTITY, and COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET merge into COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT (D15). Two tables became one, so the count is 54 tables and 4 views. Draft v5.2 (8 October 2026) adds the four decisions of the review of the v5.1 draft (D16–D19) and a set of editorial corrections; no table is added or dropped.

D13 — No return group

Decision. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group. Attribution of a return or hop leg is inherited from its parent leg. Offsets are defined between a leg's attributed group and the group of a counterparty receiver.

Rejected alternative. A dedicated group of kind = return per project holding the sender_return receivers (ERD v4.0 §6; config schema rule "one default and one return group").

Why. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not an entitlement rule, and RECEIVER.kind already enforces it. The return group (a) made every project have at least two groups, so the Understanding document's "a project with a single group never has an offset" was false by construction; (b) classified every refund as a cross-group payout under the v4.0 offset definition, triggering Management approval and offset aging; (c) left the return group's entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7, unless a reattribution path was added. Removing it restores the Understanding document's §3.3 and §6.3 wording without change. The return group entered during the v4.0 write-up; decision D3 of the review record relied on it and is amended there.

Changed tables

TableChange
RECEIVER_GROUP− kind. A group is a group; exactly one is_default per project (D13).
RECEIVERgroup_id required when kind = counterparty, null otherwise. sender_return and partner_transit receivers never appear on forward deals or allow lists (validation on kind) (D13).
DEALreceiver_group_id: set at quote on the first forward leg; a return leg inherits it from its parent leg, leg n of a route from leg n−1 (D13).
DISBURSEMENT_LINEA line paying a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group and is never an offset (D13).
RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT+ account_kind (bank / wallet); details_ref → bank_details_ref (bank accounts only); + network, + address (wallets only). Write-time rule: a bank account has bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet has network and address and a crypto rail matching the network (D14).

D14 — Explicit wallet fields on receiving-entity accounts. Rejected: keeping wallet details inside the opaque details_ref. Why: the collection side already stored network and address explicitly; the payout side did not, so addresses could not be validated, checked against the rail, or queried across partners. Bank details stay external by reference, as before.

D15 — Partner entity and collection endpoint

Decision. FACILITATING_ENTITY is renamed PARTNER_ENTITY: the partner's legal vehicle whose name appears on paperwork, the mirror of RECEIVING_ENTITY on the client side. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY (bank-in) and WALLET (crypto-in) merge into one COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT table owned by a partner entity, with kind = bank / wallet and the field shape of RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (rail required only on active bank endpoints, see D18). COLLECTION points at one endpoint (collection_receiving_endpoint_id, null for cash) instead of the hand-rolled endpoint_type + endpoint_id pair. The rename is pending NPL confirmation; the FRS term "Facilitating Entity" stays in Appendix A.1.

Rejected alternative. Keeping two endpoint tables, one with a legal owner (wallets under a vehicle) and one without (bank accounts directly under the partner config).

Why. A bank account is always in some legal entity's name, so the v4.0 split left the schema unable to say which vehicle owns a bank-in account, while every wallet knew its owner. One endpoint table under the vehicle fixes the asymmetry, lets the system check that the account a sender paid into belongs to the vehicle stamped on the deal, removes a polymorphic pair from COLLECTION, and makes the partner side read exactly like the client side: config → entity → endpoint.

TableChange
PARTNER_ENTITYrenamed from FACILITATING_ENTITY; − bank_details_ref (moved to its endpoints).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINTnew; replaces COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET. partner_entity_id, kind (bank / wallet), currency, bank_details_ref (bank), network + address (wallet), status.
COLLECTIONendpoint_type + endpoint_id → collection_receiving_endpoint_id (null for cash).
DEALfacilitating_entity_id → partner_entity_id.
Invariant 6adds: a collection's endpoint must belong to the leg's partner entity.

v5.2 — decisions of the review of the v5.1 draft (8 October 2026)

D16 — Registration payout details follow the account's kind

Decision. SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION gains network and address (nullable). bank_details_ref ("as paid by this partner") is set only when the registered account's account_kind is bank; for a wallet account the registration carries the network and address as the partner registered them, and the bank field stays empty. The registration remains the partner's view of the destination; RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT remains NPL's.

Rejected alternative. Keeping a bank-only field on wallet registrations (the v5.1 shape).

Why. After D14 and D15 every other destination record is kind-aware; a wallet registration had no field that fitted, so an approved wallet destination either carried no details or carried an address in a field named for bank details. Storing the partner's copy also lets the system compare NPL's record with the partner's before paying to a wallet, where a wrong address is unrecoverable.

D17 — DISBURSEMENT_LINE.deal_id

Decision. DISBURSEMENT_LINE gains deal_id, a nullable foreign key to DEAL: required when the paid receiver is group-less (sender_return, partner_transit), optional on counterparty lines. New invariant 19. GROUP_ENTITLEMENT reads the paying leg's group from it.

Rejected alternative. Leaving the rule in prose ("a payout to a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group").

Why. A DISBURSEMENT pools many deals, and neither it nor its lines named one; the D13 rule and the view that depends on it could not be computed from stored columns, and invariant 7 could not be checked mechanically. The same column will carry the per-line discharge facts of the scenario in which a EUR invoice is paid in USDT in parts.

D18 — Nullable rail on COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT

Decision. The endpoint gains rail, nullable. Null means "not yet known", never "does not matter": a bank endpoint cannot become active — and no COLLECTION or payment instruction may reference it — until rail is set; a wallet endpoint may leave rail null (its network already names the road), and when rail is set on a wallet it must match network (mirrors D14).

Rejected alternative. A NOT NULL rail, which forces a guessed value when a partner sends incomplete details; or no rail at all (the v5.1 shape), which made the "same field shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT" claim inexact.

Why. The road matters on the collection side as much as on the payout side: the same EUR account reachable by SEPA or SWIFT needs different instructions and arrives with different fees; local rails carry transaction limits (UPI caps, RTGS minimums); and a wrong rail recorded with confidence causes the failures a blank cannot.

D19 — Endpoint kind must match the leg's collection method

Decision. A write-time rule, added to invariant 6: a collection endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method — wallet for crypto-in, bank for bank-in, and cash-in has no endpoint.

Rejected alternative. None; the rule was missing.

Why. After D15 the fact "how does the money arrive" lives in two places — DEAL.collection_method and the endpoint's kind — and nothing stopped them disagreeing silently.

DISBURSEMENT_LINE+ deal_id — nullable FK to DEAL; required when the paid receiver is group-less, optional on counterparty lines (D17).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT+ rail — nullable; required before a bank endpoint becomes active; on a wallet, must match network when set (D18).
COLLECTIONNo column change: may reference only an active endpoint whose kind matches the leg's collection_method (D18, D19).

The small gaps noted in the engagement record (EXCEPTION entity, PARTNER_STATEMENT, configuration versioning, SENDER_CREDIT.applied_to_deal_id, DEAL_GROUP.estimate_out, cash rounding per currency, operating time zone) are not addressed in v5.2 and remain open.

7 · Open questions

2 of the questions carried from the Understanding document remain open; the rest were answered by NPL in the review of the Understanding document or settled in the ERD reviews of 6–8 October 2026 and are reflected in this draft.

Still open

#QuestionBlocksStatus
9FRS figure reconciliation (1,208 vs 1,225; Mode 1 example)Golden casesSud: Needs clarification. To be discussed.
11Reference workbooks per project archetypeCalculation acceptanceSud: Will be added soon.

Answered and reflected in v5.2

#QuestionAnswerIn the model
1Collect-first: must SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW pre-exist for attribution; handling of inbound matching no senderSud: Yes, sender-receiver mapping should be done in configuration. When the transaction is created, the sender is picked from a list.v4.0: write-time rule that a collect-first deal needs an existing allow entry; the allow list now targets receiver groups.
2Withholding-eligibility criteria on rerouted dealsReview (7 Oct): NPL’s cut is always captured at conversion, so it is never at risk from a return or a forward. If forwarding happens before conversion, whichever partner converts captures it.v4.0: the eligibility question dissolves. forwarding_policy is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues; withhold_earnings is removed. Ownership flips at one event only.
3Post-collection reroute (funds stuck at a partner): transfer, offset, or refund-and-requoteSud: The partner can send the funds to NPL (and NPL decides where to send) or the partner can refund the sender.v4.0: REROUTE.outcome via_own_wallet / refund_sender; a refund is a return leg paying the sender_return receiver.
4Receiving-entity constraints (currency, rail) narrowing settlement choiceSud: Receiving entities have specific bank accounts with currency and rail restrictions, for example EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA.v4.0: RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT; registrations and payout lines point at the account.
5Any deliberate partial-disbursement / reserve policySud: Yes, possible. In some projects the client’s funds sit until they are ready to receive them, within an exposure threshold NPL sets by appetite.v4.0: PROJECT.disburse_policy to_zero / hold_allowed with exposure_ceiling as the cap; invariant 4 restated.
6Receiver-side fee timing per projectSud: Receiver-side fee should be applied at the time of conversion, otherwise the balance will be incorrect.v4.0: default at_conversion; CONVERSION.fee_receiver_part; DISBURSEMENT_LINE.receiver_fee_applied becomes exceptional.
7Network-fee policy on refundsSud: Set at project level with per-transaction override (one 100 USD fee was repaid in the next settlement).v4.0: PROJECT.network_fee_policy plus FEE_DECISION for the override.
8Whole-unit conversion rounding ruleReview (7 Oct): fractions are dropped to whole units at conversion, per transaction (30.152 → 30). The dropped fraction stays client money, carried in the balance and paid out when it reaches a whole unit. Cash collections round to the nearest 100 / 500 / 1000 by currency.v4.0: CONVERSION.rounding_residual; CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding and cash_rounding_unit; disburse to less than one unit; SHORTFALL no longer takes rounding.
10AQN-LT-Sub “settled by offset against transactions outside the system”Sud: This is NPL’s wallet (pass-through at collection or on the settlement side). AQN is Aquanow, a crypto exchange; LT Sub is the account name.v4.0: OWN_WALLET.provider and account_label; pass-through is a two-leg route or a reroute via the own wallet.
12FRS P1 / P3 vs rerouting and multi-partner use — amend FRS or restrict scopeSud: Check the added explanations (partner types and channels; pass-through and double conversions in §7.1.1). Ask again if still unclear.v4.0: two-leg routes are deal groups with two legs and a partner_transit receiver for the hop; FRS principles generalised, scope kept.
13Advance funding sourceReview (7 Oct): never. NPL does not pay a receiver before the client’s money has arrived.v4.0: LEDGER_ACCOUNT purpose ADVANCE removed; the advance approval and the “advance” ownership-flip event removed.
14Review point: entitlement split on a balance conversionReview (7 Oct): chosen group, not proportional. The conversion is triggered by a specific payout.v4.0: BALANCE_CONVERSION.receiver_group_id; excess over the group’s source-currency entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
15Review point: refunds to a third party at the sender’s requestReview (7 Oct): allowed by exception only. Default is the sender’s own return receiver; any other destination needs Management approval with a reason and a pre-registered approved receiver.v4.0: invariant on return legs; APPROVAL action refund_to_third_party.
16Review point: recover dues on a rerouteReview (7 Oct): yes, NPL nets what a partner owes it against funds about to be forwarded to that partner.v4.0: forwarding_policy forward_and_recover_dues, recovered_amount, partner_agreement_ref; postings own wallet cash ← earnings receivable, no income.
17Review point: legs of a route share one client-facing quoteReview (7 Oct): yes, a deal group. The sender saw one price and one reference; margin across legs is the group quote minus the partner conversions.v4.0: DEAL_GROUP; every deal belongs to a group, a single-partner deal being a group of one leg.
18Review point (v5.0): does a refund need its own receiver group?Review (7 Oct, New XP): No. Refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule; a dedicated return group made every project multi-group (so “a single-group project never has an offset” was false by construction), classified every refund as a cross-group offset needing Management approval, and left its entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7.v5.0 (D13): sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less; return and hop legs inherit the parent leg’s attribution; offsets are defined only against counterparty groups. New invariant 18.
19Review point (v5.1): restructure the partner collection side — rename FACILITATING_ENTITY, merge the endpoints?Review (8 Oct, New XP): yes. A bank account is always in some legal entity’s name, so the v4.0 split could not say which vehicle owned a bank-in account while every wallet knew its owner. The rename to PARTNER_ENTITY is pending NPL confirmation; the FRS keeps “Facilitating Entity”.D15: FACILITATING_ENTITY → PARTNER_ENTITY (bank_details_ref moved to its endpoints); COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET merge into COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT (kind bank / wallet, same shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT); COLLECTION points at one endpoint (null for cash); invariant 6 adds that a collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity.

Appendix A · FRS reconciliation

A.1 Vocabulary

FRS termModel entity
ClientPROJECT
Receiving EntityRECEIVING_ENTITY (member of a counterparty RECEIVER, which belongs to a RECEIVER_GROUP) with its RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNTs
SenderSENDER with SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW; its refund destination is a group-less sender_return RECEIVER
Partner (PT, Jeton)PARTNER + PARTNER_CONFIG
Facilitating Entity / Wallet registryPARTNER_ENTITY with its COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINTs (kind = bank / wallet) (D15)
Rate-day versionsRATE_COMPARISON + PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
SettlementDISBURSEMENT + DISBURSEMENT_LINE + CONFIRMATION (+ DISBURSEMENT_RETURN when rejected)
Shortfall ledgerSHORTFALL + CL.<RECEIVER>.<CCY>.SHORTFALL
PT Comms / H CommsCO.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.POOL (earnings receivable)
Inter-entity redirectionOffset across receiver groups: a counterparty paid_receiver_id in another group than the paying leg’s
Double conversion / pass-throughDEAL_GROUP with two legs (funding_source = prior_leg), hop via a group-less partner_transit RECEIVER

A.2 Deviations from the FRS (classified)

FRS statementModelClassification
P1 — no custodyNo custody in the normal path; OWN_WALLET + REROUTE for contingencyDecision required (Q12)
P3 — partner books never mixAccounts per partner never net; alternate partner on reroute; post-collection transfer only if Q3 confirmsDecision required (Q12)
Strict Client → Entity → Sender, one parent eachRECEIVER_GROUP → RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → account; SENDER with a group allow-list; FRS project = one default groupGeneralisation per NPL instruction
Beyond grace → re-quote alwayslate_collection_policy per project; FRS project keeps requotePer NPL instruction (Sept 2026)
Sender always priced on KrakenFEE_STRUCTURE.rate_basis; FRS project = marketGeneralisation
One settlement per deal, full amountAccumulate → disburse to less than one unit (whole units; rounding dust carried), or hold within the exposure cap where the project allowsGeneralisation
Partner fixed at quoteSame, except under REROUTEConsistent
Bank fee → shortfall → top-upcarry_forward is the FRS behaviour; waived / absorbed addedPer NPL instruction
Registry-only destinationsSETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION.approval_status — FRS project has all approvedGeneralisation
AQN-LT-Sub offset-settled collectionsOWN_WALLET at Aquanow; pass-through is a two-leg deal group or a reroute via the own walletResolved (v4.0)
